newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-OVERNIGHT RATES SEEN DIPPING, LAT/DOLLAR STABLE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-OVERNIGHT RATES SEEN DIPPING, LAT/DOLLAR STABLE.

text.p: Latvian overnight rates were seen slipping over the weekend ahead of the end of the month liquidity scramble and the lat/dollar rate was seen holding stable at around .570, dealers said.
Dealers said that overnight rates have been more or less steady this week, shortened by a four-day holiday, at a bid/ask of 3.50/4.50 percent.
Dealers said they expected the rates to slip by Monday as most banks were expected to have their liquidity house in order in time to meet the central bank's minimum reserve requirements.
But they cautioned that some banks were still scrambling to meet the requirements, a situation which could push the rates up.
"Rates are expected to go down a bit...but some banks are short on lats, and that could move things the other way," said one dealer.

The lat meanwhile held steady at around .570 to the dollar and dealers did not expect it to move far from its current range, citing relative stability on global currency markets and no anticipated influx of either currency into the local market.
